title: Ukraine Strikes Russia's Ust-Luga Baltic Oil Port for Sixth Time This Year
detail: Ukrainian drones struck the Novatek-Ust-Luga gas processing and transshipment complex in Russia's Leningrad Oblast overnight, sparking a fire and damaging two processing units, according to Ukraine's General Staff and Leningrad Oblast Governor Alexander Drozdenko. Ust-Luga is Russia's largest Baltic Sea oil-export port, handling roughly 700,000 barrels a day, and this marked the sixth Ukrainian strike on the facility since March 2026 as part of Kyiv's sustained campaign against Russian energy export revenue. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed 553 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight across multiple regions; no casualties were reported at Ust-Luga. Separately, Russian guided aerial bombs killed at least two people and injured 17 in Kramatorsk and the nearby village of Bilenke.

title: Russian Double Drone Strike on Home in Buryn, Sumy Oblast, Kills Mother and 9-Year-Old Son
detail: Russian forces struck a private residential house in the Buryn community of Sumy Oblast with two attack drones in a targeted double strike early on August 14, killing a 29-year-old woman and her 9-year-old son and causing extensive destruction and a fire. Four others — including the boy's father and grandmother — were injured and hospitalized with severe burns, according to Sumy Regional Military Administration head Oleh Hryhorov. The strike came amid a broader wave of 39 Russian attacks on 28 Sumy Oblast settlements over the same 24-hour period, using guided aerial bombs, drones, artillery, and rocket systems.
